decisions.mark: states that by default the macro RENAMES the member to private_<member>, and that defining MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS makes it expand to the member name unchanged
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "By default it expands to `private_##member`, so a field such as `mbedtls_aes_context::MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(nr)` ... is declared as `private_nr`." and "If it is defined, the macro expands to the bare member name." | WHY: The answer states both the default rename to private_<member> and the unchanged member name when MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS is defined.

decisions.mark: explains that the two branches give different consumers different views — code that defines MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS sees plain member names while an ordinary consumer of the public headers sees the renamed ones
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "If the symbol is not defined, `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE` renames the member. If it is defined, the macro expands to the bare member name." and "The guard only constrains outside users. Any external code that defines `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` before including the headers gets the same access" | WHY: The answer states that defining the symbol yields bare member names (library, sample programs, external code that defines it), while ordinary consumers of the public headers get `private_`-renamed names.

decisions.mark: concludes that this enforces API opacity at COMPILE time by breaking the member name, rather than by hiding the struct layout — the fields remain visible and sized
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "By default it expands to `private_##member`, so a field such as `mbedtls_aes_context::MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(nr)` ... is declared as `private_nr`. Code that writes `ctx.nr` then fails to compile. The struct layout and the header stay the same, but the names are hidden from ordinary callers. The header is not an encapsulation boundary at runtime; it is a compile-time guard on the field names." | WHY: The answer says the macro renames the member to `private_nr`, so access by the old name fails at compile time. It also says the struct layout and header stay the same, which means the fields stay visible and the layout is not hidden.

decisions.mark: conveys that the macro is applied at a scale of many hundreds of sites, overwhelmingly in the public headers rather than in library implementation
